title: SHIBOYUGI: Playing Death Games to Put Food on the Table Anime Gets Sequel
content:
Kadokawa announced on Sunday that SHIBOYUGI: Playing Death Games to Put Food on the Table , the television anime of writer Yūshi Ukai and artist Nekometal 's Playing Death Games to Put Food on the Table ( Shibō Yūgi de Meshi o Kuu ) light novel series, will get a sequel work. The company did not reveal the format of the new anime, but did reveal an early teaser visual.

SHIBOYUGI: Playing Death Games to Put Food on the Table debuted on January 7, and the first episode was 60 minutes long. Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it aired, and is also streaming an English dub . Netflix is also streaming the anime.

Crunchyroll also streams the film in North America, Central America, South America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, and the Indian subcontinent. Other streaming services like QIYI, MUSE, Aniplus , and more are streaming the film in various countries in Asia.

The film's story continues from the series, after Yuuki overcomes the "thirty-game-jinx," the arbitrary (yet nevertheless real) number of games where long-time survivors of the games begin to have drastically reduced rates of survival.

The film features a returning staff. Sōta Ueno ( Days With My Stepsister ) directed the anime at Studio DEEN . Rintarou Ikeda ( The Seven Deadly Sins: Dragon's Judgement ) was in charge of series composition. Eri Osada ( Blade & Soul ) designed the characters. Noriyoshi Konuma ( The Dangers in My Heart ) was the sound director. Junichi Matsumoto composed the music.

Yen Press licensed the light novel series and describes the story:

Yuuki wakes up to find herself wearing a maid's uniform in a strange manor. After wandering into the dining room, she comes across five other girls, each in the exact same outfit. Soon, the girls learn that the manor is brimming with lethal weapons and an array of deadly traps...and that they can only escape by playing the most gruesome of games. As the terrifying truth sets in, each girl's face goes pale—except Yuuki's. Why? Because this isn't her first go-round. That's right—Yuuki is a professional death game player who lives off the prize money she collects from winning brutal killing competitions, and she's not about to let this chance pass her by.

Kadokawa 's MF Bunko J imprint published the light novel series' first volume in November 2022, after the series won the Excellence Award at the 18th MF Bunko J Light Novel Newcomer Award that same year. The novels' 10th volume shipped on June 25, and the 11th volume will ship on December 25.

The light novel series also ranked #1 in the New Title category of Takarajimasha 's 2024 Kono Light Novel ga Sugoi! (This Light Novel Is Amazing!) rankings.

Banzai Kotobuki Daienkai launched a manga adaptation in Kadokawa 's Comp Ace magazine in April 2023. Kadokawa published the manga's sixth volume on July 23.

title: 20 Years Ago, Bleach’s Dub Forever Changed a Major Plot Twist & Fans Didn’t Even Notice
content:
Bleach Episode 62 features some of the most crucial moments in the entire series. The episode was originally released in Japan on December 20th, 2005, before getting its English release on September 8th, 2006. However, the English dub carried a subtle yet crucial change from the original version that forever ruined a major plot twist of the story. The debate centering around anime subs and dubs has been going on for decades, and there’s really no way to determine which is overall better. Many English-speaking fans find it easier to follow through with a story in a language they are familiar with rather than reading subtitles constantly.

Anime from the 1990s and 2000s especially relied on English dub during TV broadcasts to attract more viewers in the West. Unfortunately, there have been many such cases where the dubs fail to capture the true essence of the story. This is also the case for Bleach, where the dub of Episode 62 changed a crucial moment between Gin and Rangiku. They’re two of the most beloved characters in the series, especially Gin, who became even more popular after the truth behind his actions came to light in the Fake Karakura Town . However, fans watching the dub missed a crucial hint that Episode 62 dropped before he bid farewell to Rangiku.

Bleach English Dub Changed Gin’s Apology to Rangiku

The Soul Society Arc is often considered to be one of the best parts of the story, especially since this is when the series gets more intense. Bleach expands its world-building and introduces Sosuke Aizen as one of the most dangerous villains in the story. Along with Aizen, two Squad Captains also betrayed the Soul Society, including Gin Ichimaru. Initially portrayed as a villain, it wasn’t until the Fake Karakura Town that the series revealed Gin only wanted to defeat Aizen by any means necessary. He also wanted to get back the fragment of the Soul King Aizen stole from Rangiku.

During Episode 62, Rangiku tries to stop Gin from leaving Soul Society, but the Menos Grande from Hueco Mundo emits a light called Negacion that would seriously injure other Soul Reapers if they touch it. Gin quickly pushed her away so she wouldn’t get hurt, but also didn’t forget to taunt her that he didn’t mind being her prisoner for a little while longer. However, things actually became more interesting when he said, “Maybe next time.” This is completely different from the subbed version where he actually apologizes to her.

Gin also couldn’t hide the sorrow on his face, so saying, “I’m sorry,” actually made a lot more sense in that moment. The subbed version also puts into perspective that betraying Rangiku deeply hurt him, but there wasn’t another path he could’ve chosen. Not only that, but this scene also makes fans realize that Gin wasn’t always portrayed as a heartless snake. The hints were always there, which is all the more reason the plot twist was so heartbreaking yet exceptionally well-written.

Did you notice the difference between the Bleach sub and dub in Gin’s farewell to Rangiku? Do you think the change affected the emotional impact of the scene? Share your thoughts in the comments.

title: 'Kekkaishi no Ichirinka' Reveals Additional Cast, Staff, Opening Theme, First Promo
content:
The official website of the Kekkaishi no Ichirinka ( Bride of the Barrier Master ) television anime revealed additional cast, staff, a key visual (pictured), the opening theme, and first promotional video on Sunday. The anime series adapting Kureha 's romantic supernatural novel is scheduled to premiere on January 6 at 11:00 p.m. on Tokyo MX, followed by BS Nippon Television, Sun TV, and other stations.

Voice actors Chiaki Kobayashi ( Sousou no Frieren ) and Takuya Eguchi ( Spy x Family ) are joining the cast as Yanagi Ichise and Yukizasa Sankourou, respectively.

Staff Chief Animation Director: Minami Murayama ( Atri: My Dear Moments prop design) Art Director: Kouki Nagayoshi ( Re:Creators ), Hiromi Bandou ( Himegoto ) Color Design: Ami Hayashi ( Yatogame-chan Kansatsu Nikki Yonsatsume ) Director of Photography: Tomomi Kawai ( Nigashita Sakana wa Ookikatta ga Tsuriageta Sakana ga Ookisugita Ken ) CG Director: Masaya Machida (Stimulus Image) ( Chou Kaguya-hime! ) 3D Works: Mitsutaka Iguchi ( IDOLiSH7 ) Editing: Shouta Migiyama ( Aldnoah.Zero ) Sound Director: Takatoshi Hamano ( Yani Neko ) Sound Effects: Noriko Izumo ( Grand Blue )

Music group Naniwa Danshi ( Nintama Rantarou Movie: Dokutake Ninja Tai Saikyou no Gunshi ending theme) is performing the opening theme "Ichirinka," which previewed in the first promotional video below.

Tooru Kitahata ( Nihon e Youkoso Elf-san. ) is directing the anime at TROYCA , with Yuuko Kakihara ( Giji Harem ) handling the series composition and script. Minami Murayama is designing the characters. Yukari Hashimoto ( Komi-san wa, Comyushou desu. ), Ruka Kawada ( Toumei Otoko to Ningen Onna ), and R・O・N ( Tensei shitara Dainana Ouji Datta node, Kimama ni Majutsu wo Kiwamemasu ) are composing the music.

Kureha published the romantic supernatural novel under its Kadokawa Bunko imprint in December 2021, featuring illustrations by Bodax . The seventh volume was released on June 16.

Odayaka began drawing a manga adaptation in B's-LOG Comic magazine in May 2020. Kadokawa published the eighth volume on July 30.

J-Novel Club licensed both the light novel and manga in English release in August 2022 and July 2023, respectively. The fourth light novel volume shipped on July 15, with the fifth volume scheduled for a December 8 release. The sixth manga volume went on sale on May 26, with the seventh volume scheduled to be released on February 23, 2027.

title: Bride of the Barrier Master Anime Reveals Main Trailer, Visual, Additional Cast, Opening Theme Song Artist
content:
To celebrate November 22nd’s “Good Spouses Day” in Japan, the main visual trailer for Bride of the Barrier anime have been released. The latest trailer features the opening theme song “Ichirinka” by Naniwa Danshi. Additionally, Chiaki Kobayashi and Takuya Eguchi will join the series as additional cast members as Yanagi Ichise and Yukizasa Sankoro, respectively. Netflix will stream the anime starting on January 6, 2027, with an hour-long first episode.

Staff:

• Original Story: Kureha

• Original Character Design: Bodax

• Manga: Odayaka（B’s-LOG COMICS）

• Director: Toru Kitahata

• Series Composition & Screenplay: Yuko Kakihara

• Character Design・Chief Animation Director: Minami Murayama

• Art Director: Kouki Nagayoshi, Hiromi Bandou

• Color Design: Ami Hayashi

• Director of Photography: Tomomi Kawai

• CG Director: Masaya Machida (StimulusImage)

• 3D Works: Mitsutaka Iguchi

• Editor: Shota Migiyama

• Music：Yukari Hashimoto, Ruka Kawada, R・O・N

• Sound Director: Takatoshi Hamano

• Sound Effects: Noriko Izumo

• Animation Studio: TROYCA

• Production: Bride of the Barrier Master PARTNERS

Voice Cast:

• Hana Ichise: Akari Kito

• Saku Ichinomiya: Kikunosuke Toya

• Hazuki Ichise: Kanon Takao

• Nozomu Ichinomiya: Hiroto Shimizu

• Yanagi Ichise: Chiaki Kobayashi

• Azuha: Yuzuki Tamukai

• Aoi: Taihi Kimura

• Miyabi: M・A・O

• Yukizasa Sankoro: Takuya Eguchi

Synopsis: Since time immemorial, Japan has been protected from external enemies by 5 pillars. Born into a branch family of a clan of practitioners that protect the pillars, since childhood, Hana Ichise has been disdained, continuously compared to her talented older twin sister. One day, Hana is suddenly awakened to a great power, but in order to live a peaceful life, she chooses to conceal her power and lives as a failure of a practitioner. However, the young head of the main clan, Saku Ichinomiya, discovers her power and pressures her into getting married…？ Will Hana be able to attain her dream of a quiet and peaceful life? This is the story of a neglected girl’s journey to finally live as her true self. Source: Press Release, Official Website ©Kureha, Bodax, Odayaka/KADOKAWA/Bride of the Barrier Master PARTNERS

title: Bride of the Barrier Master TV Anime Reveals 1-Hour Debut on January 6, More Cast in Video
content:
The staff for the television anime of Kureha 's Bride of the Barrier Master ( Kekkaishi no Ichirinka ) light novel series revealed the anime's January 6 debut, opening theme song, more cast, new visual, and main promotional video on Sunday.

Naniwa Danshi performs the opening theme song "Ichirinka," which can be heard in the above video.

The anime will debut on January 6 at 11:00 p.m. on Tokyo MX , and will have a one-hour special debut. The series will also stream on Netflix at the exact same time it debuts on Tokyo MX .

The series will also air on many other channels in Japan including BS NTV , Sun TV , KBS Kyoto , and more. The anime will also stream on other services in Japan, but after the Netflix stream debuts.

The new cast includes Chiaki Kobayashi as Yanagi Ichise and Takuya Eguchi as Yukizasa Sankoro.

The anime will star:

• Akari Kitō as Hana Ichise

• Kikunosuke Toya as Saku Ichinomiya

• Kanon Takao as Hazuki Ichise

• Hiroto Shimizu as Nozomi Ichinomiya

• Yuzuki Tamukai as Azuha

• Taihi Kimura as Aoi

• M.A.O as Miyabi

Tōru Kitahata ( Science Fell in Love, So I Tried to Prove It , Welcome to Japan, Ms. Elf! , Hinako Note ) is directing the anime at TROYCA . Minami Murayama ( ATRI: My Dear Moments six episodes, IDOLiSH7 Third Beat! three episodes animation director) is designing the characters, and Yūko Kakihara ( Blue Box , Cells at Work! , 2022 & 2024 Urusei Yatsura ) is in charge of the series scripts. Yukari Hashimoto ( Mr. Osomatsu , Penguindrum ), Ruka Kawada ( Is the order a rabbit? , Isekai Quartet ), and R.O.N ( Kusunoki's Garden of Gods , FLCL Alternative ) are composing the music.

Yen Press ' Yen On imprint publishes the light novels in English and describes the story:

For thousands of years, Japan has been protected by five clans wielding barrier-weaving magic. Born to a branch family of one such clan, eighteen-year-old Hana has always been stuck in the shadow of her more capable, beautiful, and popular twin sister. When a strong power awakens within Hana, she chooses to hide it so she can continue living a quiet life out of the spotlight. But that ideal lifestyle begins to slip out of reach when Saku Ichinomiya takes over as the new head of the Ichinomiya clan and sets out to find a bride strong enough to stand by his side. Eager to keep her abilities secret, Hana steers clear of Saku... but will she be tempted to sign a marriage contract if it guarantees the peaceful, quiet future of her dreams?

Kadokawa published the novels' first volume with Bodax 's illustrations in December 2021, and it published the seventh volume on June 16. The novels have over 2.5 million copies in circulation.

Odayaka 's manga adaptation launched on Kadokawa 's B's-LOG COMIC digital manga magazine in March 2022. Kadokawa will publish the manga's ninth compiled book volume on December 28. Yen Press also publishes the manga adaptation in English.

title: After 31 Years, This Legendary Sci-Fi Anime Movie Still Has No Worthy Competition
content:
During a career spanning over forty years, Mamoru Oshii became a pioneering anime director and filmmaker, best known for his incredible work in the Ghost in the Shell franchise. While the legendary director has been a part of the industry since the 1980s, he got his global breakthrough thanks to the Ghost in the Shell film in 1995. The film not only became a massive hit in Japan, but it made Oshii globally renowned after catching the attention of fans in the United States and Europe. Oshii is particularly famous for his distinctive , philosophy-oriented storytelling, along with artistic style, sometimes even prioritizing visuals over the plot.

Before his greatest sci-fi movie, he made his directorial debut in 1983 with the Urusei Yatsura: Only You film, and then released another film of the franchise in the following year. Ghost in the Shell premiered in Japan on November 18th, 1995, exactly 31 years ago. It’s safe to say that the film has had no worthy competition over the decades. This also applies to the anime remake by Science SARU , which was one of the biggest hits of the year. While the remake was a more faithful adaptation of the acclaimed manga by Masamune Shirow, Oshii took liberties in his storytelling, making it stand out from other anime.

Ghost in the Shell Movie Can’t Be Recreated Today

Due to the advancement in technology, modern animation has changed significantly over the years. Unlike the animation from a few decades ago, animators rely mostly on a blend of traditional hand-drawn animation with digital techniques, primarily using CGI for lighting, coloring, backgrounds, and motion. This allows the animators to include more details in each frame, creating a unique sense of depth and aesthetic appeal. However, while modern animation has its perks, it’s evident that modern technology can’t create such intricate details as seen in the older anime , especially something as artistic as Ghost in the Shell .

The film is a pioneer of new animation techniques, known for its stunning visuals through the use of a blend of traditional cel animation with early computer-generated imagery. The anime industry largely moved from traditional cel animation to digital pipelines in the early 2000s, completely changing the art style and the grainy visuals that fans appreciate from the 1990s anime even now. Not to mention that Ghost in the Shell is one of those rare cases where changes from the manga can be seen as a more intriguing method of storytelling, especially if you realize what kind of vibe Oshii was going for.

Oshii’s adaptation took a much darker tone than the original manga, especially with the protagonist Motoko Kusanagi. Although she is more cheerful in the manga, her personality in the movie suited the intense themes in the movie, especially considering its futuristic setting. It wasn’t just her, but the overall manga had a much more cheerful and warm vibe, all the while portraying the problems within the futuristic society.

Do you think any modern sci-fi anime has come close to matching Ghost in the Shell ? What makes this legendary sci-fi movie so timeless? Share your thoughts in the comments!

contentBlocks.text: During a career spanning over forty years, Mamoru Oshii became a pioneering anime director and filmmaker, best known for his incredible work in the Ghost in the Shell franchise. While the legendary director has been a part of the industry since the 1980s, he got his global breakthrough thanks to the Ghost in the Shell film in 1995. The film not only became a massive hit in Japan, but it made Oshii globally renowned after catching the attention of fans in the United States and Europe. Oshii is particularly famous for his distinctive , philosophy-oriented storytelling, along with artistic style, sometimes even prioritizing visuals over the plot.

Before his greatest sci-fi movie, he made his directorial debut in 1983 with the Urusei Yatsura: Only You film, and then released another film of the franchise in the following year. Ghost in the Shell premiered in Japan on November 18th, 1995, exactly 31 years ago. It’s safe to say that the film has had no worthy competition over the decades. This also applies to the anime remake by Science SARU , which was one of the biggest hits of the year. While the remake was a more faithful adaptation of the acclaimed manga by Masamune Shirow, Oshii took liberties in his storytelling, making it stand out from other anime.
Ghost in the Shell Movie Can’t Be Recreated Today

Due to the advancement in technology, modern animation has changed significantly over the years. Unlike the animation from a few decades ago, animators rely mostly on a blend of traditional hand-drawn animation with digital techniques, primarily using CGI for lighting, coloring, backgrounds, and motion. This allows the animators to include more details in each frame, creating a unique sense of depth and aesthetic appeal. However, while modern animation has its perks, it’s evident that modern technology can’t create such intricate details as seen in the older anime , especially something as artistic as Ghost in the Shell .

The film is a pioneer of new animation techniques, known for its stunning visuals through the use of a blend of traditional cel animation with early computer-generated imagery. The anime industry largely moved from traditional cel animation to digital pipelines in the early 2000s, completely changing the art style and the grainy visuals that fans appreciate from the 1990s anime even now. Not to mention that Ghost in the Shell is one of those rare cases where changes from the manga can be seen as a more intriguing method of storytelling, especially if you realize what kind of vibe Oshii was going for.

Oshii’s adaptation took a much darker tone than the original manga, especially with the protagonist Motoko Kusanagi. Although she is more cheerful in the manga, her personality in the movie suited the intense themes in the movie, especially considering its futuristic setting. It wasn’t just her, but the overall manga had a much more cheerful and warm vibe, all the while portraying the problems within the futuristic society.

title: Classroom of the Elite Season 5 Announces 2027 Premiere Date
content:
It was announced at the MF Bunko J Autumn School Festival event that Classroom of the Elite Season 5 is set to premiere in 2027. A teaser visual and trailer were also released. Season 5 was officially announced immediately after the fourth season’s finale premiered.

The anime is an adaptation of Shogo Kinugasa’s Classroom of the Elite light novels. The first season premiered in 2017 and had 12 episodes. Season 2 was announced in March 2022, and it ran for 13 episodes in the Summer 2022 anime season. Season 3 was delayed from its original schedule and ended up premiering in January 2024, also getting a total of 13 episodes. Season 4 aired from April to June 2026.

Crunchyroll is streaming the anime, and they describe the story: Kiyotaka Ayanokoji has just enrolled at Tokyo Koudo Ikusei Senior High School, where it’s said that 100% of students go on to college or find employment. But he ends up in Class 1-D, which is full of all the school’s problem children. What’s more, every month, the school awards students points with a cash value of 100,000 yen, and the classes employ a laissez-faire policy in which talking, sleeping, and even sabotage are permitted during class. One month later, Ayanokoji, Horikita, and the students of Class D learn the truth of the system in place within their school…

title: 'Youkoso Jitsuryoku Shijou Shugi no Kyoushitsu e 5th Season: 2-nensei-hen 2 Gakki' Airs in 2027
content:
The MF Bunko J Autumn School Festival 2026 revealed cast members, main staff, and a teaser visual (pictured) for Youkoso Jitsuryoku Shijou Shugi no Kyoushitsu e 5th Season: 2-nensei-hen 2 Gakki ( Classroom of the Elite 5th Season: Second Year, Second Semester ) on Sunday. The first part of the fifth season adapting Shougo Kinugasa 's 2-nensei-hen ( Year 2 ) sequel light novel will premiere in 2027.

Cast Kiyotaka Ayanokouji: Shouya Chiba ( 86 ) Suzune Horikita: Akari Kitou ( Mato Seihei no Slave ) Kei Karuizawa: Ayana Taketatsu ( Kanojo mo Kanojo ) Kikyou Kushida: Yurika Kubo ( Haite Kudasai, Takamine-san ) Kakeru Ryuuen: Masaaki Mizunaka ( Tsue to Tsurugi no Wistoria ) Honami Ichinose: Nao Touyama ( Bokutachi no Remake ) Arisu Sakayanagi: Rina Hidaka ( Kage no Jitsuryokusha ni Naritakute! ) Tsubasa Nanase: Minako Satou ( Jibaku Shounen Hanako-kun ) Kazuomi Housen: Hiroya Egashira ( Ragna Crimson ) Ichika Amasawa: Momoko Seto ( Uma Musume: Cinderella Gray ) Takuya Yagami: Shinnosuke Tokudome ( Kijin Gentoushou ) Sakurako Tsubaki: Iori Saeki ( Shokei Shoujo no Virgin Road ) Riku Utomiya: Shougo Sakata ( Chiyu Mahou no Machigatta Tsukaikata ) Miyabi Nagumo: Souma Saitou ( Yuukoku no Moriarty )

Staff Director: Noriyuki Nomata ( Danganronpa 3: The End of Kibougamine Gakuen - Zetsubou-hen assistant director) Series Composition: Kou Shigenobu ( Youkoso Jitsuryoku Shijou Shugi no Kyoushitsu e 3rd Season ) Character Design: Maki Kouno ( Bokura wa Minna Kawai-sou ), Haruna Nagata ( Kuzu no Honkai animation director) NEW , Saori Yonemoto ( Jibaku Shounen Hanako-kun 2 Part 2 animation director) NEW Sound Director: Satoki Iida ( Paripi Koumei ) Studio: Lerche

The first three seasons adapting Kinugasa's school psychological light novel —also known by its short title You-Zitsu —aired in Summer 2017 , Summer 2022 , and Winter 2024 , followed by the fourth season adapting the sequel light novel in Spring 2026. Crunchyroll streamed the first season with subtitles, with Funimation streaming an English dub. Crunchyroll also simulcasted the second, third, and fourth seasons.

MF Bunko J imprint released the original light novel in 14 volumes between May 2015 and September 2019, featuring illustrations by Shunsaku Tomose ( Ange Vierge ). Kinugasa launched the 2-nensei-hen ( Year 2 ) sequel light novel in January 2020, concluding it with 15 volumes in November 2024. He subsequently began penning the 3-nensei-hen ( Year 3 ) sequel in March 2025. Kadokawa published the fifth volume on October 23.

Yuyu Ichino began drawing a manga adaptation of the first light novel in Monthly Comic Alive magazine in January 2016. Kadokawa released the 12th volume in February 2022.

Xia Sasane serialized a manga adaptation of the sequel light novel from December 2021 to December 2024. The fourth and final volume went on sale in January 2025.

A third manga adaptation subtitled 2-nensei-hen - 2nd Stage by Hachi Komada began serialization in January 2025. Kadokawa released the second volume on April 23, with the third volume scheduled for a December 22 release.

Seven Seas Entertainment licensed both the light novel and manga adaptation in English in July 2018 and June 2021, respectively. The second volume of the sequel went on sale on September 1, with the third volume going on sale on December 29. The 12th and final manga volume went on sale in November 2024.

title: Classroom of the Elite Anime's 5th Season Reveals Full Title, Visual, 2027 Debut
content:
Kadokawa revealed on Sunday the title, teaser visual, teaser visual video, and 2027 debut for the fifth season of the Classroom of the Elite television anime. The title is Yōkoso Jitsuryoku Shijō Shugi no Kyōshitsu e 5th Season 2-nen Sei Hen 2 Gakki [Zen Han] (Classroom of the Elite 5th Season: Second Year, Second Semester [First Half]).

Noriyuki Nomata is returning from the fourth season to direct the fifth season at Lerche . Kou Shigenobu is also returning to oversee the series scripts. Satoki Iida is returning as the sound director. Maki Kōno is returning as character designer. Also credited as fellow character designers on the fifth season are Saori Yonemoto and Hina Nagata , who were both chief animation directors on the fourth season.

Crunchyroll streamed the season as it aired, and also streams an English dub.

The cast members from the previous seasons reprised their roles in the fourth season. The new cast for first-year students included:

• Minako Satō as Tsubasa Nanase

• Hiroya Egashira as Kazuomi Hōsen

• Momoko Seto as Ichika Amasawa

• Shinnosuke Tokudome as Takuya Yagami

• Iori Saeki as Sakurako Tsubaki

• Shōgo Sakata as Riku Utsunomiya

Noriyuki Nomata ( Kujima Utaeba Ie Hororo ) directed the fourth season at Lerche , and Kou Shigenobu ( Classroom of the Elite , Boruto: Naruto Next Generations ) was in charge of series scripts. Shigenobu also wrote the scripts with Kyōko Katsuya ( Boruto: Naruto Next Generations , Classroom of the Elite ). Maki Kōno ( The Kawai Complex Guide to Manors and Hostel Behavior ) designed the characters. Satoki Iida ( Classroom of the Elite , Amagami SS ) was the sound director. Masaru Yokoyama ( Classroom of the Elite , Freezing ) and Kana Hashiguchi ( Classroom of the Elite , Young Ladies Don't Play Fighting Games ) composed the music at Lantis .

The first season premiered in July 2017. Crunchyroll streamed the season, and Funimation streamed an English dub.

The second and third seasons adapt the original story's complete first-year-student arc. The second season premiered in July 2022. Crunchyroll streamed the season as it aired under the title Classroom of the Elite II . The third season premiered in January 2024 and aired for 13 episodes, concluding the first-year arc. Crunchyroll again streamed the season as it aired in Japan.

title: Solo Leveling’s Biggest Competitor Is Making a Huge Comeback Ahead of Anime Premiere
content:
There’s no denying that Solo Leveling is the most popular and influential webtoon and light novel series of all time. It also paved the path for the entire medium’s success across the globe, encouraging more animation studios to release webtoon adaptations. This is all thanks to the success of the anime adaptation by A-1 Pictures, as it became one of the biggest hits in history. Solo Leveling isn’t the first manhwa to get an anime adaptation, but no South Korean series pushed the medium to this level of global popularity as it did. Following the second season’s conclusion last year, the anime announced its sequel movie during this year’s Anime Expo.

However, while fans await the anime’s return, its biggest competitor is also planning a huge comeback. Along with Solo Leveling, Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint is often considered just as globally renowned. The series has already confirmed an anime adaptation in 2024, and it’s already one of the most anticipated series right now. While the anime is currently under production, the webtoon is ongoing, and it’s all set to return with its anticipated second season.

What Is the Release Date of Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint Season 2?

Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint will be released on November 24th, 2026. The official X handle of REDICE Studio only shared the Korean release date, along with a 30-second teaser. The first season of the webtoon went on a hiatus in May this year with the release of Chapter 311. The season ends on a huge cliffhanger, as it marks a major turning point in the series while stopping near the end of the Demon King Selection arc. The second season will kick off from where the story left off and wrap up the ongoing arc before moving on to the next one.

The webtoon has already adapted almost half of the web novel, so if the second season releases around the same number of chapters, then this will be the final season of the series. While the series is returning with a new season for Korean fans, the English platform Webtoon is also continuing to release the translations after several months. The serees went on a hiatus after the English release of Chapter 308 in June this year, but the next chapter was finally released on November 21st, 2026. We can expect the remaining two chapters to drop on the platform before the English debut of Season 2.

Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint Anime Hasn’t Shared Any Updates Yet

Although it’s been more than two years since the anime adaptation was announced, fans still have no idea when it will be released. Previously, the anime was expected to debut in 2027, but a report by Com2uS’ website confirmed the wait will be longer than expected. While the report shared by Com2uS stated that the anime adaptation of ORV was slated for 2028, it hasn’t been officially confirmed by major distributors or production partners, leaving its status uncertain for now.

The anime was officially announced on July 7, 2024, at the Crunchyroll Industry Panel, which means the streaming platform for the anime has already been decided. ORV is expected to be a major hit after the anime debut, especially since it shares the same system trope, similar to the beloved action series, Solo Leveling .

Are you excited for the return of the Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint webtoon? What are your expectations for the second season?
